summary: Targeted MOBILE responsiveness audit across 9 URLs (/, /insights/, /virtual-site-visits/, /property-sales-technology-trends/, /property-agent-technology/, /contact/, /privacy-policy/, /terms-conditions/, /404.html) at 4 widths (375, 390, 414, 768). Result: NO horizontal overflow on ANY page at ANY width — document.documentElement.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth for all 36 combinations. Body font-size is 16px on every page. Header (logo + hamburger/Start-a-Project) and footer render within viewport with no clipping. The only element wider than the viewport is `.rfm-marquee` (react-fast-marquee scrolling ticker on /) which is by design contained inside a parent with computed `overflow: hidden` — so it does NOT cause page overflow (verified: parent width = viewport width, doc scrollWidth = viewport width). Static/legal pages (/contact/, /privacy-policy/, /terms-conditions/, /404.html) render cleanly with padded containers.

issues: Micro 'eyebrow' labels use font-size 9.6px (e.g. classes text-[0.6rem]: 'SCROLL', '360°', 'QUALIFIED ENQUIRY'). These are stylistic ALL-CAPS mono labels, not body text, but 9.6px is below the commonly recommended 10-11px floor for readability on mobile. Body/paragraph text is 16px and reads fine.
The hero sub-paragraph beneath 'EXPERIENCE.' appears low-contrast (dark orange/brown on near-black background) — legible but not high-contrast. Consider lightening.

The WhatsApp CTA element found in DOM is `position: static` (rendered near the bottom of the very long landing page, bottom offset ~14344px). The task brief describes a 'sticky WhatsApp button' — if the intent is a fixed floating action button that stays visible while scrolling, the current implementation is NOT sticky/fixed. Not a mobile-overflow issue, but worth confirming with product intent.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Bump the 0.6rem (9.6px) eyebrow labels to 0.65rem (10.4px) or 0.7rem (11.2px) — matches the other eyebrows and improves mobile legibility.
OPTIONAL: Confirm whether the WhatsApp CTA is meant to be a fixed/sticky floating button. Currently it renders inline (position: static) at the end of the page.
critical_code_review_comments: Mobile responsiveness is solid: no overflow, no offending elements, containers properly clipped. .rfm-marquee is correctly wrapped in an overflow:hidden parent — good pattern for scrolling tickers.
Insights .container (max 760px, padding 0 22px) is behaving well at 375/390/414/768 — text reflows without touching edges.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (mobile audit: 36/36 URL×width combinations pass with zero horizontal overflow)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Mobile is FULLY responsive at 375/390/414/768 across all 9 pages. If user reports 'not responsive', ask them for (a) exact device/browser, (b) URL, (c) screenshot — the codebase itself has no overflow issues. Only two minor discretionary items: (1) 9.6px eyebrow micro-labels on landing, (2) WhatsApp CTA is static-positioned inline rather than a fixed floating button. Use page.evaluate to compute documentElement.scrollWidth vs window.innerWidth for objective overflow checks.
